references.text: Moses repeats the instruction to collect gifts for the tabernacle, including gold, silver, and copper, as voluntary offerings from the people.
Describes how the people brought gold, silver, and copper as offerings to the Lord, fulfilling the command in Exodus 25:3.
Summarizes the gifts of silver and gold given at the dedication of the altar, showing the same pattern of valuable metals as offerings.
David collects gold, silver, and copper for the building of the temple, paralleling the collection of materials for the tabernacle.
The people give gold, silver, and other valuables for the rebuilding of the temple after the exile, echoing the tabernacle's collection.
Ezra receives gold, silver, and copper as gifts for the house of the Lord, in the same tradition as the offerings to the tabernacle.
Theological parallel: The principle of building God's house through voluntary gifts of silver and gold is repeated from the wilderness to the temple.
Theological contrast: Gold and silver as holy offerings (Exodus) versus corrupt treasures (James).
